title: CASPIAN — THE DAY THE SILENCE SANG

lyrics.note: Lyrics are archived for provenance but are not used to direct this version of the film.

genre.label: Reggae Dubstep Mix
genre.user_declaration: this is a Reggae Dubstep Mix

rhythm.pulse_description: Fast nominal pulse with a heavy half-time directing feel; major material motion follows ~76 BPM while fine texture can respond to faster subdivisions.
rhythm.meter_or_groove: Reggae/dub offbeat feel fused with dubstep half-time weight and bass-led section dynamics.

sections.narrative_function: Hold a dark near-static sculptural field with barely perceptible internal life.
Introduce the first warm fissure and begin localized material invasion/reconstruction.
Expand from one portrait/material state into a richer abstract living surface while preserving a stable compositional anchor.
Make the material behave more fluidly: ripple, ring, fold, reflect and reorganize without literal scenery.
Contract to a smaller, denser visual state and prepare the long high-energy transformation.
Drive the main metamorphic passage: pressure, flex, split, merge and re-form the image through multiple coherent states using hybrid source/generated stills.
Slow the transformation and allow visual echoes/afterimages of prior states to coexist in one composition.
Nearly stop the image; preserve only micro-motion, breath and faint warm light.
Rebuild the dark field into its most complete metamorphic state, merging source-frame and generated visual identities into one resolved abstract form.
Let the transformed surface release, dim and simplify until one restrained point/fissure of light remains before black.

directing_rules: Music is the sole narrative/timing authority for this version; lyrics are excluded by current-user instruction.
Use ~76 BPM half-time weight for primary deformation and faster subdivisions only for fine texture.
Reggae offbeat may create sway, recoil and delayed visual echo; dubstep accents may create localized pressure and depth, never whole-frame shake.
Major transformations follow phrase/section structure, not every beat.
Abstract material continuity is more important than literal story imagery.
